title: Telegram command mentions are not normalized before routing
original_report: In the family Telegram group, selecting /tasks from the command menu sends /tasks@familyhealtheee_bot. The bot does not open the task list, while plain /tasks works.
discovery_scope: Telegram security, lifecycle, context, planning, and task-list tests

candidates.candidate: Telegram command mention is not normalized before routing
candidates.contract: Registered Telegram commands must route the same whether Telegram appends the current bot username or not.

candidates.candidate: Commands addressed to another bot must not be processed by Family AI
candidates.contract: A generic handler must ignore known commands addressed to a different bot.

expected: The current bot's mention form is normalized to /tasks and routed to the planner; a foreign-bot mention is ignored; ordinary text containing @ is unchanged.
actual: The mention form reached the generic router as an unrecognized command and was classified as general.
reproduction: The focused regression test compares plain and mentioned forms for all registered commands, verifies foreign-bot safety, and verifies ordinary @ text.
failure_signal: Before the fix, the own-bot mention assertion failed with assert 'general' == 'planner'; after the fix, all 14 focused cases pass.
root_cause: _routing_text() only recognized an exact command token such as /tasks. Telegram's @bot_username suffix made the token different, so the generic handler did not route it to the planner.
fix_summary: Added one shared registered-command list, normalized own-bot mentions before orchestration, ignored known commands addressed to other bots, and reused the list for the Telegram command menu.
why_causal: The generic handler now converts /tasks@familyhealtheee_bot to /tasks before domain routing, while the handler exits before authorization and orchestration for a different bot mention.

reproduction_files.summary: Approved regression coverage for own-bot, foreign-bot, all registered commands, and ordinary @ text.

fix_files.summary: Shared command registry and mention normalization used by the generic handler and command menu.

limitations: The Telegram API always supplies valid bot usernames using Latin letters, digits, and underscores; the regression uses a valid foreign-bot username.
The test suite emits an existing google.genai deprecation warning.
residual_risks: If Telegram does not return a bot username during startup, mentioned commands are conservatively not normalized.
notes: No dependencies, secrets, authorization policy, or Railway configuration were changed.
Commit and push were intentionally not performed in this fix pass.
